salient

SAY-lee-unt -- stress on the first syllable, SAY. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Salient is standing out as the most noticeable and important.

Her report opened with the most salient fact: the bridge had failed inspection three years in a row.

Example

On a slide crowded with numbers, the designer prints one figure in red type five times larger than everything else, and every eye in the room goes straight to it.

That one figure is the salient detail -- it leaps out from everything around it. Salient describes the most noticeable or most important feature, the one that stands out and demands attention first.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

striking: Striking means catching attention in a dramatic, memorable way -- a striking resemblance, a striking sunset. Striking is only about the impression something makes on the eye or mind, while salient adds weight: the salient detail both stands out and matters most to the argument.

noticeable: Noticeable means simply easy to notice -- a noticeable stain, a noticeable limp. It promises nothing about importance, and that is the line salient draws: a salient fact stands out AND matters, while a merely noticeable one may catch your eye and change nothing.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

minor: lesser in importance

inconspicuous: not attracting attention

Where it sits · how much notice and weight it carries — prominent → salient → paramount

prominent vs. salient: Prominent is milder than salient -- a prominent feature is easy to see, while a salient one leaps out and organizes how you understand everything else.

paramount vs. salient: Paramount outranks salient: a salient point is the one that stands out most, while a paramount concern sits above all others in importance, whether or not it catches the eye.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — sali-

root — sali-: to leap (Latin salire)

suffix — -ent

suffix — -ent: in a state of; doing (Latin -entem)

Put it together

Put it together: Salient comes from Latin salire, 'to leap,' plus -ent -- literally 'leaping.' A salient feature is the one that leaps out at you: the detail that jumps off the page before you have read anything else.

Use the root in a new word: resilient

Use the root in a new word: resilient: The resilient sapling sprang upright again after the storm bent it flat.

Root Check

Word Choice

Salient belongs to analysis and argument: the salient points of a proposal, the salient features of a design, the most salient fact in a case. Use it for the detail that both stands out and matters -- if something is merely eye-catching but unimportant, call it noticeable instead.
